title: TypeScript Config & Declarations: Quick Revision
summary: Night-before revision notes on tsconfig compiler options (strict flags, target, module, moduleResolution, paths), declaration files and @types, declare module, and the isolatedModules and verbatimModuleSyntax flags.

chapters.title: tsconfig Mental Model
points: tsconfig.json tells tsc what to compile (include/exclude/files) and how (compilerOptions); tsc with no args finds it by walking up from the current directory
Type-checking and emitting are separate jobs: noEmit true means check only, which is the usual setup when a bundler (Vite, esbuild, SWC) emits the JS
Compiler options fall into 3 groups: strictness (what errors), output (target, module, outDir) and resolution (moduleResolution, paths, types)
Types are erased at compile time, so tsc never changes runtime behaviour or adds runtime checks; it only checks and strips

extends inherits a base config (e.g. @tsconfig/node20); the child's compilerOptions override the base, but include/exclude/files replace rather than merge, and paths inside extends resolve relative to the config that defines them

chapters.title: Strict Flags
points: "strict": true turns on the whole strict family at once; set it on every new project and opt out of single flags only if needed
strictNullChecks: null and undefined are not assignable to other types, so string | undefined must be narrowed before use; this is the flag that catches the most bugs
noImplicitAny: a parameter or variable with no inferable type is an error instead of silently becoming any

strictFunctionTypes (parameters are checked contravariantly for function-typed properties, method syntax stays bivariant), strictBindCallApply (bind/call/apply are type-checked) and strictPropertyInitialization (class fields must be assigned in the constructor or use !, requires strictNullChecks)
useUnknownInCatchVariables makes catch (e) typed unknown, so narrow with instanceof Error before reading e.message; alwaysStrict emits "use strict"

NOT in strict, enable separately: noUncheckedIndexedAccess (arr[i] and record[key] become T | undefined), exactOptionalPropertyTypes (optional prop x?: number rejects an explicit undefined), noImplicitOverride, noImplicitReturns, noFallthroughCasesInSwitch

chapters.title: target, module and moduleResolution
points: target sets the JS syntax level of the output (ES2022, ESNext); newer syntax is kept as-is and older syntax is downleveled; it does not add polyfills or library typings

lib sets the available built-in typings (e.g. ["ES2023", "DOM"]); it defaults from target, so using Array.prototype.at or fetch types without matching lib gives 'property does not exist' errors even though the runtime has them
module sets the emitted module format: CommonJS, ESNext, or NodeNext (decided per file from package.json "type" and the .mts/.cts extension)

moduleResolution decides how an import string maps to a file: node10 (legacy, ignores package.json exports), node16/nodenext (Node ESM rules: relative imports need the .js extension, honours exports), bundler (for Vite/webpack/esbuild: extensionless imports allowed, honours exports)

Pairing rules: Node app or library uses module NodeNext (moduleResolution follows automatically); bundled app uses module ESNext with moduleResolution bundler; never use moduleResolution bundler when tsc output runs directly in Node

chapters.title: paths, baseUrl and Resolution Gotchas
points: paths maps import aliases to locations, e.g. "paths": { "@/*": ["./src/*"] }; with TS 4.1+ it works without baseUrl, and relative targets resolve from the tsconfig file

paths only affects type-checking; tsc does not rewrite the specifiers in emitted JS, so the runtime or bundler needs the same alias (Vite resolve.alias, vite-tsconfig-paths, Node subpath imports or tsc-alias)
Most common alias bug: the editor is happy (paths set) but the build or node run fails 'Cannot find module' because the bundler or runtime alias was never configured
Under node16/nodenext a relative import must end in .js even though the source file is .ts, because TypeScript resolves the output name: import './util.js' finds util.ts

types: ["node"] limits which @types packages are auto-included as globals; typeRoots changes where they are searched; skipLibCheck: true skips type-checking .d.ts files, so it hides errors inside dependencies and is a normal setting but not a fix for your own types

chapters.title: Declaration Files, @types and declare module
points: A .d.ts file holds only types (no runtime code); it describes JS that exists elsewhere; the declaration flag makes tsc emit .d.ts next to the JS, and the package.json "types" field or exports "types" condition points consumers to it

@types/x (DefinitelyTyped) supplies types for a JS-only package: npm i -D @types/express; packages that ship their own types need no @types, and a missing @types gives 'Could not find a declaration file for module' (TS7016)
declare module 'untyped-lib'; in a .d.ts silences TS7016 by typing the whole module as any; to type it properly write declare module 'untyped-lib' { export function foo(x: string): number; }
Ambient wildcard modules type non-code imports: declare module '*.svg' { const src: string; export default src; } and declare module '*.css'

Module augmentation: a .d.ts that has a top-level import or export is a module, so declare module 'express' { interface Request { user?: User } } merges into the library's types; with no top-level import/export it becomes a global ambient declaration that replaces rather than augments; use declare global { } inside a module to add globals; the file must be inside include or tsc will not see it

chapters.title: isolatedModules, verbatimModuleSyntax and Cheat Sheet
points: isolatedModules: true errors on code that a single-file transpiler (esbuild, SWC, Babel, ts-loader transpileOnly) cannot compile correctly; it needs each file to be understood alone, so re-exporting a type needs export type { T } and const enum use is restricted

verbatimModuleSyntax: true makes the rule simple: imports and exports without the type modifier are kept in the output, and ones with it are erased; so import type { User } from './user' or import { type User } vanishes while import { User } of a type is an error; it also implies isolatedModules-style safety and replaces the old importsNotUsedAsValues and preserveValueImports
verbatimModuleSyntax caveat: a file using ESM import/export syntax is an error when emitting CommonJS (module CommonJS); use module NodeNext with a CJS package or write import x = require('x')

Recommended modern baseline: strict true, noUncheckedIndexedAccess true, target ES2022, module ESNext, moduleResolution bundler, verbatimModuleSyntax true, skipLibCheck true, noEmit true (bundled app); for a Node package use module NodeNext instead

Cheat sheet error map: TS7016 means add @types/x or declare module; 'Cannot find module' means check moduleResolution and the bundler alias for paths; TS2307 on a .js-suffixed relative import means NodeNext rules; 'Object is possibly undefined' means strictNullChecks or noUncheckedIndexedAccess is working as intended, so narrow instead of using !
